This Flight Manual provides operating limitations, normal procedures, emergency procedures, and technical information for the safe operation of the HayesX-250 electric Vertical TakeOff and Landing (eVTOL) aerial vehicle.
Manufacturer: HayesX Inc.  Las Vegas, Nevada, US
Category: Single-Seat Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing Aerial Vehicle
The HayesX-250 is a single-seat electric vertical takeoff and landing aerial vehicle utilizing a quadrotor-octocopter configuration.
The HayesX-250 is designed, built, and operated in accordance with the US FAA Part 103 Regulations and CCAR-91-R4 Requirements for Ultralight Vehicles.
Under these Regulations, the HayesX-250 is classified as an Ultralight Vehicle and accordingly:
Certification as a conventional aircraft is not required

The aircraft parachute has a 6-year validity period.  At the expiry of the period, please contact the aircraft manufacturer for inspection.  This entire aircraft rescue system is a pyrotechnic device and must be disassembled and/or repaired by authorized personnel only.
HayesX-250 shall be operated only under Visual Flight Rules (VFR).
The pilot shall maintain continuous visual awareness of surrounding airspace, terrain, obstacles, and other aircraft.
Flight is permitted only under Visual Meteorological Conditions (VMC).
HayesX-250 is approved for daytime operations only.
Night operations are prohibited unless specifically authorized by the applicable aviation authority.

3.13 Parachute Activation Procedure (Ballistic Recovery System BRS)

The parachute is deployed by the pyrotechnic driven piston system.  The pre-flight checklist should ensure that the parachute red cover is unobstructed.  Deployment of the BRS to be undertaken in the following situations:
Stop using joystick and/or digital flight controls
Pull the red start parachute handle on the left
Wait for parachute to fully deploy
It is not approved or recommended for HayesX-250 to be flown over water
In the event that you are flying over water and you have a catastrophic event, please follow the emergency procedure:
Brace for impact with the water
Turn off power immediately after contact with the water surface
Unfasten your seat belt and evacuate
In the event the pilot is somewhat incapacitated, has a panic attack, or is otherwise unable fly the aircraft, every effort should be made to immediately to:
To land the aircraft automatically with Auto Land, press the PFD automatic landing button.
To return to home, press the PFD return to home button.
If unable to operate Auto Land or Return to Home, activate the BRS.

4.4.1 High Voltage System Safety Check - General
HayesX-250 utilizes a dual 108V DC electrical power system.
The front and rear battery packs are connected to the aircraft’s main power system through QS12 high-voltage connectors.
High-voltage system maintenance shall only be performed by trained personnel.
QS12 connectors undamaged and in good condition
Locking mechanism is normal and functional
Do not connect or disconnect QS12 connectors under electrical load.
Do not operate with damaged connectors.
If any of the following occurs:
Disconnect power immediately and discontinue operation.
